text.p: Electrical engineering group ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG said it was in negotiations with an Indian company, Videocon Power, to build and take an equity stake in a 1,050 megawatt coal-fired power plant near the city of Madras.
"I can confirm that we are in negotiations with a company, Videocon Power, and our interest is in coal-fired plant," an ABB spokesman said in response to inquiries.
The Indian newspaper Economic Times first reported that ABB was in talks to build the power plant near Madras.
"The discussions are whether to join as equity partner," the spokesman added.
The newspaper said ABB was interested in a 45 percent equity stake in the power plant, but the ABB spokesman declined to comment further on ABB's possible stake.
"This is still under negotiations," the spokesman said.
The newspaper said the value of the power plant would be $1.2 billion and one of the largest power projects in India.
The spokesman confirmed the value of the plant would be around $one billion.
